threads.body: [General] The `HttpClient` created on every `record` call is never closed, leaving its engine and coroutine resources alive after each test. Scope it with `use` so cleanup also occurs when the request or assertions fail.

+import kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking
+import org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test
+import org.junit.jupiter.api.extension.RegisterExtension
+
+class KtorClientHeadersTest {
+
+  companion object {
+    @JvmStatic
+    @RegisterExtension
+    private val testing = LibraryInstrumentationExtension.create()
+
+    private val REQUEST_HEADER = AttributeKey.stringArrayKey("http.request.header.x-test-request")
+    private val RESPONSE_HEADER = AttributeKey.stringArrayKey("http.response.header.x-test-response")
+    private val SECRET_REQUEST_HEADER = AttributeKey.stringArrayKey("http.request.header.x-test-secret")
+  }
+
+  @Test
+  fun `selector patterns capture headers that are not listed by name`() {
+    val span = record { telemetryBuilder ->
+      telemetryBuilder.requestHeaders(
+        IncludeExclude.builder().setIncluded("X-Test-*").setExcluded("*-secret").build()
+      )
+      telemetryBuilder.responseHeaders(IncludeExclude.builder().setExcluded("Content-*").build())
+    }
+
+    assertThat(span.attributes.get(REQUEST_HEADER)).containsExactly("request-value")
+    assertThat(span.attributes.get(RESPONSE_HEADER)).containsExactly("response-value")
+    // excluded patterns take precedence over included patterns, and header matching is
+    // case-insensitive
+    assertThat(span.attributes.get(SECRET_REQUEST_HEADER)).isNull()
+  }
+
+  @Test
+  fun `deprecated captured headers capture headers listed by name`() {
+    val span = record { telemetryBuilder ->
+      @Suppress("DEPRECATION") // testing the deprecated API
+      telemetryBuilder.capturedRequestHeaders("X-Test-Request")
+      @Suppress("DEPRECATION") // testing the deprecated API
+      telemetryBuilder.capturedResponseHeaders("X-Test-Response")
+    }
+
+    assertThat(span.attributes.get(REQUEST_HEADER)).containsExactly("request-value")
+    assertThat(span.attributes.get(RESPONSE_HEADER)).containsExactly("response-value")
+  }
+
+  private fun record(configure: (TestKtorClientTelemetryBuilder) -> Unit): SpanData {
+    val telemetryBuilder = TestKtorClientTelemetryBuilder()
+    telemetryBuilder.setOpenTelemetry(testing.openTelemetry)
+    configure(telemetryBuilder)
+    val instrumenter = telemetryBuilder.buildInstrumenter()
+
+    lateinit var request: HttpRequestData
+    val client = HttpClient(MockEngine) {
+      engine {
+        addHandler { requestData ->
+          request = requestData
+          respond("", HttpStatusCode.OK, headersOf("X-Test-Response", "response-value"))
+        }
+      }
+    }
+    val response = runBlocking {
+      client.get("http://localhost/test") {
+        header("X-Test-Request", "request-value")
+        header("X-Test-Secret", "secret-value")
+      }
+    }
+
+    val context = instrumenter.start(Context.root(), request)
+    instrumenter.end(context, request, response, null)
+
+    return testing.spans().single()

replies.body: Good catch — fixed in d9974a3. `record` now builds the client as `HttpClient(MockEngine) { ... }.use { client -> ... }`, with the request and the `instrumenter.start`/`instrumenter.end` calls moved inside the block so the engine and its coroutine scope are closed even when the request or the assertions throw.

threads.body: [General] `DefaultHttpClientInstrumenterBuilder#setCapturedRequestHeaders` converts this collection into an `IncludeExclude` selector, so `*` and `?` are treated as globs rather than literal names (the shared API test at `instrumentation-api/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/api/semconv/http/HttpHeadersTest.java:169` explicitly verifies that behavior). Consequently these deprecated Ktor compatibility methods can capture unintended headers and contradict their new documentation. They need an exact-name capture path; the response and `Iterable` overloads have the same issue.

replies.body:
This is reading a stale copy of the base branch, and I verified that rather than assuming it.

`DefaultHttpClientInstrumenterBuilder#setCapturedRequestHeaders` no longer builds an `IncludeExclude`. On the base branch `trask/http-header-selectors-api` it routes through `CapturedHttpHeaders.createExact`, which stores the names in a literal set and never constructs a selector. The `HttpHeadersTest` case you cite was renamed and inverted at the same time: `deprecatedCapturedHeadersSettersTreatStarAsEveryHeader` is gone, and `deprecatedCapturedHeadersSettersMatchHeaderNamesLiterally` now sits at that line asserting the opposite. Copilot reviews the head branch in isolation, so it doesn't see base-branch commits; CI builds `refs/pull/N/merge` and does.

The evidence, from `refs/pull/19608/merge` (`f572922c8c`, merging `d9974a3483` into base `1572a0077b` — exactly what CI compiles):

```
io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.ktor.common.v2_0.KtorClientHeadersTest: tests=3 failures=0
   - deprecated captured headers match names literally()
```

That test calls `capturedRequestHeaders("*")` and `capturedResponseHeaders("*")` and asserts that `http.request.header.x-test-request`, `http.request.header.x-test-secret` and `http.response.header.x-test-response` are all absent — i.e. `"*"` looks for a header literally named `*` and finds nothing, even though the getters enumerate every header name. Run against the head branch alone it fails with `expected: null but was: ["request-value"]`, which is precisely the widening you describe; it passes on the merge ref. The `Iterable` overloads share the same one-line delegation, and `AbstractKtorServerTelemetryBuilder` is covered by `KtorServerCapturedHeadersTest` in ktor-2.0.

So the documented literal-matching promise is implemented, and there is a regression test that fails loudly if the globbing path is ever reintroduced.

threads.body: [General] `DefaultHttpServerInstrumenterBuilder#setCapturedRequestHeaders` now builds a glob-matching `IncludeExclude`, so a legacy value such as `*` captures every enumerated Ktor header instead of a header literally named `*`. This violates the compatibility behavior documented here and can expose additional headers. Add/use an exact-name capture path for all request/response and `Iterable` compatibility overloads in this class.

Same stale-base reading as the client builder thread, and I verified it against the merge ref rather than assuming.

`DefaultHttpServerInstrumenterBuilder#setCapturedRequestHeaders` does not build a glob-matching `IncludeExclude` on the base branch this PR targets; it routes through `CapturedHttpHeaders.createExact`, which keeps the names as a literal set. Copilot reviews the head branch in isolation and so doesn't see that commit; CI builds `refs/pull/N/merge` and does.

Server-side proof, from `refs/pull/19608/merge` (`f572922c8c`):

```
io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.ktor.v2_0.KtorServerCapturedHeadersTest: tests=1 failures=0
```

That test configures the plugin with `capturedRequestHeaders("X-Test-Request", "*")`, sends both `X-Test-Request` and `X-Test-Secret` against a real Netty-backed Ktor server, and asserts that `http.request.header.x-test-request` is captured while `http.request.header.x-test-secret` is absent. If `"*"` were globbing, the secret header would be on the span, since `KtorHttpServerAttributesGetter` enumerates every request header name. All four request/response and `Iterable` overloads here are one-line delegations to the same two exact-name setters, so they share that behavior.

Same stale-base reading as the two `ktor-common-2.0` threads. `builder.setCapturedRequestHeaders` no longer converts the list to an `IncludeExclude`; on the base branch this PR targets it routes through `CapturedHttpHeaders.createExact`, which stores the names literally and never builds a selector. Copilot reviews the head branch in isolation, so base-branch commits are invisible to it; CI builds `refs/pull/N/merge` and picks them up.

I verified rather than assuming: `KtorClientHeadersTest.deprecated captured headers match names literally` and `KtorServerCapturedHeadersTest.testDeprecatedCapturedHeaders` both pass on `refs/pull/19608/merge` (`f572922c8c`), and the former fails with `expected: null but was: ["request-value"]` against the head branch alone — the widening you describe, present only when the base fix is missing.

The ktor-1.0 setters here are the same one-line delegation to the same exact-name path, and `KtorServerCapturedHeadersTest` in this module covers the deprecated route end to end through a real Netty-backed server. I deliberately dropped the `ReplaceWith` on these deprecations for a related reason: it would be an automated IDE rewrite that silently migrates a user's literal `"*"` into a globbing selector with no diff to inspect.
